# dch_C27_2466

**Rule.** 3|n -> n/3; n mod 27 = 1,10,14,19,23,26 -> n+1; 16 -> n+2; 5,20 -> 2n+1; 2,7,8,13 -> 2n-1; 25 -> 4n+1; 11 -> 4n-1; 4,22 -> 5n+1; 17 -> 5n-1.

As a table map (Q = 27): n mod 27 in {0,3,6,9,12,15,18,21,24} -> (n)/3; n mod 27 in {1,10,14,19,23,26} -> n+1; n mod 27 in {2,7,8,13} -> 2n-1; n mod 27 in {4,22} -> 5n+1; n mod 27 in {5,20} -> 2n+1; n mod 27 in {11} -> 4n-1; n mod 27 in {16} -> n+2; n mod 27 in {17} -> 5n-1; n mod 27 in {25} -> 4n+1.

**Question (GLOBAL).** Is every positive orbit eventually periodic, and what are the cycles?

**Answer.** Yes. There are exactly 3 cycle(s): (1 2 3), (5 11 43 45 15), (125 624 208 209 419 420 140 281 1123 1125 375).

**Status.** PROVED (Theorem 2 of dichotomy.md, with the integer certificate below). depth record: every plain descent certificate needs 2466 steps; near-critical cycle 80/81.

## Proof

(H1), (H2) and (P) hold, so Theorem 1 of dichotomy.md applies. decide.py found integer weights c(r) for r mod 27 with c(s)·u_r < c(r)·w_r on every edge r → s of the residue graph. The weights have 60-bit size and are printed by `python3 decide.py --id dch_C27_2466`. Each of the 45 edge inequalities is checked with integers, and the largest edge ratio is θ = 0.998928 < 1. By Theorem 2, V(n) = c(n mod 27)·n strictly decreases except on the finite set F = {n : V(Tn) ≥ V(n)}. F is contained in {n ≤ 1863} (symbolic bounds N_r) and has 332 elements, the largest being 1852. Every orbit meets F and every cycle meets F. Iterating each element of F until it repeats gives exactly the cycles listed above. ∎

## Difficulty

* The minimal stopping depth is **k\* = 2466** (Theorem 3). Every plain descent certificate T^j(n) < n on residue classes needs some class with j ≥ 2466, and one with max j = 2466 exists. The minimal certificate has 134469124803824924327 leaves when residues mod 27 are distinguished.
* Witness for the lower bound: the progression n ≡  (mod ) (modulus has 1424 bits). On it, T^i(n) ≥ n for every i < 2466 at all large n. `check_systems.py` verifies this at n = a + M·10^12 by direct iteration.
* The reason is the max-mean cycle of the residue graph: length 11, multiplier 80/81 ≈ 0.987654, mean log-multiplier -0.001129 per step. It contracts, but only barely, so by Theorem 3(c) the depth is large. The a-priori depth bound from the potential is 4632.
* A one-step weighted potential nevertheless proves GLOBAL, so on the census scale this is tier 2 (descent plus a finite table). The depth matters only for plain certificates. For comparison, the round-2 depth record desc_s32_max has k = 44.

**Novelty.** I know of no prior occurrence of this specific map; novelty was not checked beyond that. The census catalogue and round 2 do not contain it.

**Check.** `check_systems.py` (all systems, about 5 s).
